1.why: verify-token enforces record.sessionId === session.id so the token is bound to the requesting session, though accountBinding is a fixed constant rather than a true per-user binding.

2.why: False — a token issued to one session fails verification in any other session because of the sessionId binding check.

3.why: True — the password endpoint performs no session invalidation or rotation, so all existing sessions in the Map (including the resetting one) remain valid until their 1-hour expiry.

4.why: TLS is configured in Bun.serve, non-HTTPS requests are rejected and HSTS is set, but no explicit TLS min/max version pins the 'latest' version.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests and passwords are bcrypt-hashed (strong hashing rather than encryption), and contact data is never persisted.

6.why: The mock delivery message contains only the token and no private user data, and responses are generic, so no private data is exposed via the message.

7.why: Inputs are validated (contact control-char/length check, strict token regex, JSON size/structure limits) and output is rendered via textContent only, though contact validation itself is minimal.

8.why: The application has no redirects or external URLs at all; only same-origin paths are handled and CSP enforces form-action/connect-src 'self'.

9.why: There are no email templates and no user input is ever rendered as HTML or script — textContent only, nonce-based CSP, and '<' escaped in the injected JSON state.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the recovery token and MFA code are written to the browser 'Logs' panel and console via localLog, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA confirmation code is hardcoded as '482916' directly in the source, so a secret code is stored in the code.

12.why: No default user accounts or credentials exist and password policy is enforced, but the fixed MFA code '482916' functions as a constant, default-like code for every session.

13.why: Multiple layers block repeated wrong attempts: recovery limited to 3/15min, verification to 6/10min, 5 attempts per token, and MFA locks for 60s after 5 failures.

14.why: The recovery endpoint returns the identical generic message ('If the contact can be used for recovery...') regardless of whether the contact is recognized.

15.why: The token is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues (random and complex) and bound to the session, but the accountBinding is a static constant so it is not bound to a distinct user account.
